scenario: Regression baseline for the --strict-on-hard-a51 opt-in failure mode (implemented in v1.1.16, Sprint 1 / T6 via scripts/promote_strict_preflight.py + hooks/pre_bash_promote.sh). Under --strict-on-hard-a51, /bsa-promote MUST refuse to land canonical when any A51 row with BlockingStatus=hard + ResolutionStatus=open exists without an H4 waiver. The fixture's canonical state has exactly one such row (A51-CONFL-003) so the strict-mode pre-flight check fires.
_spec_only_history: Was true through v1.1.15 (orchestrator did not honor --strict-on-hard-a51). Flipped to false in v1.1.16 when the implementation landed.

expected_default_mode_verdict._comment: Default permissive mode (no --strict-on-hard-a51) accepts hard-blocking A51s as long as evidence-binding + audit markers pass. The contract is 'surface as A51', not 'block on contradictions'.

expected_invariants: EXACTLY ONE A51 row with BlockingStatus=hard + ResolutionStatus=open exists
Both contradicted A59 claims point at the same A51 ref (A51-CONFL-003)
No H4 waiver for A51-CONFL-003 (handoff is not even emitted in this fixture; the spec scenario is pre-handoff promote)
ClaimStrength=0.0 on both contradicted claims (same-tier neutralization)
expected_negative_invariants: Default-mode promote on this fixture PASSES the F5/identity hooks (contradicted claims are correctly captured); the BLOCK is opt-in only.

Removing --strict-on-hard-a51 (or unsetting BSA_STRICT_ON_HARD_A51) MUST drop back to default permissive mode — pinned by tests/test_promote_strict_preflight.py::test_hook_default_mode_skips_preflight.
